steps.title: Import Angular modules and dependencies
steps.instruction: Import CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module names and paths. These modules are needed for form handling in Angular.
steps.seedCode: // Import CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules for forms are imported, enabling form functionality in the application.
successCriteria: CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule are imported from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular modules for form handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but check if all required ones (CommonModule, FormsModule, ReactiveFormsModule) are present with correct paths.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Ensure you import CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.

steps.title: Create the main form component
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component named MultiStepFormComponent with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. Set the selector to 'app-multi-step-form' and template to an empty string for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A MultiStepFormComponent class with @Component decorator is created, ready for form logic.
successCriteria: MultiStepFormComponent is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-multi-step-form', and empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the base component structure. Next, we'll add the form logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Ensure the component has the @Component decorator with selector 'app-multi-step-form' and an empty template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't set up correctly. Review Angular component basics: use @Component decorator with selector and template.

steps.title: Define the form steps interface
steps.instruction: Inside the MultiStepFormComponent class, define a TypeScript interface named FormStep with id (number), title (string), and completed (boolean) properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a FormStep interface that defines the structure for each step in your multi-step form.
successCriteria: A FormStep interface is defined with id: number, title: string, and completed: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the FormStep interface with proper type safety.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has all three required properties with correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormStep interface isn't properly defined. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword and included all three properties with correct types.

steps.title: Initialize the steps array
steps.instruction: Inside the MultiStepFormComponent class, create a property called 'steps' that is an array of FormStep objects. Initialize it with three empty step objects, each having a 'title' and 'completed' property.
steps.hint: Define a property with the syntax 'steps: FormStep[] = [ ... ];' inside the component class. Each object in the array should match the FormStep interface structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'steps' property containing three form step objects, ready to be used in the multi-step form UI.
successCriteria: The 'steps' property is defined as an array of FormStep objects and initialized with three objects, each having 'title' and 'completed' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the steps array with three form step objects. This provides the data structure needed to track progress through the multi-step form.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started setting up the steps array, but make sure it's properly typed as FormStep[] and contains exactly three objects with 'title' and 'completed' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The steps array initialization is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create a 'steps' property inside the component class, type it as FormStep[], and initialize it with three objects matching the FormStep interface.

steps.title: Create current step index state
steps.instruction: Inside the MultiStepFormComponent class, add a property named 'currentStepIndex' with type 'number' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Add this property after the steps array property. Use TypeScript type annotation to specify it's a number.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a property tracking current page
currentPage: number = 0;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a property to track which step the user is currently viewing.
successCriteria: The MultiStepFormComponent class contains a 'currentStepIndex' property of type number initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the current step index state. This will allow us to track which step the user is currently viewing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is named 'currentStepIndex', has type 'number', and is initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The current step index state wasn't added correctly. Look at the instruction again and try adding the property as specified.

steps.title: Define next step handler
steps.instruction: Inside the MultiStepFormComponent class, add a nextStep() method that increments currentStepIndex and marks the current step as completed.
steps.hint: You can access the current step using this.steps[this.currentStepIndex]. Set its completed property to true before incrementing the index.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a nextStep() method that properly advances to the next step and updates the current step's completion status.
successCriteria: A nextStep() method is defined that increments currentStepIndex and sets the current step's completed property to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the nextStep() method to navigate forward through the form steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a nextStep() method, but make sure it both marks the current step as completed and increments the index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nextStep() method is missing or doesn't properly handle step navigation and completion.

steps.title: Define previous step handler
steps.instruction: Inside the MultiStepFormComponent class, add a method named previousStep that decrements the currentStepIndex property by 1, but only if currentStepIndex is greater than 0.
steps.hint: You can create a method that checks if currentStepIndex > 0 before decreasing it. Use this.currentStepIndex-- to decrement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method to safely navigate to the previous step in the form.
successCriteria: A previousStep method exists that decrements currentStepIndex when it's greater than 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the previousStep method. This allows users to navigate backward through the form steps safely.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a previousStep method, but make sure it properly checks that currentStepIndex is greater than 0 before decrementing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The previousStep method is missing or doesn't correctly decrement currentStepIndex when appropriate. Try adding a method that decreases currentStepIndex only when it's greater than 0.

steps.title: Add step navigation structure
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a <div> container that uses *ngFor to iterate over the steps array and display each step's title and completion status.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let step of steps" to loop through the steps. Display step.title and step.completed inside the div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying items with *ngFor

{{ item.name }} - {{ item.status }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A navigation UI structure is created that will display each step's title and completion status when the component renders.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> with *ngFor="let step of steps" that displays step.title and step.completed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the step navigation structure using *ngFor.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using *ngFor to iterate over the steps array and displaying both the title and completion status.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step navigation structure is missing or incorrect. You need to add a <div> with *ngFor that displays each step's title and completion status.

steps.title: Create step content container
steps.instruction: In your component's template, add a <div> element with *ngIf to display content only when currentStepIndex equals 0 (for the first step).
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngIf structural directive to conditionally render the div based on the current step index.
steps.analogousExample: // Conditional display based on index
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element will be added that conditionally displays content for the first step.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a container that will show content for the first step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but make sure it has the correct *ngIf condition to check currentStepIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step content container is missing or incorrect. Add a <div> with *ngIf to conditionally display based on currentStepIndex.

steps.title: Add navigation buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the step content container, add two buttons: one labeled 'Previous' that calls the previousStep method when clicked, and one labeled 'Next' that calls the nextStep method when clicked. Make sure the 'Previous' button is disabled when currentStepIndex is 0.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click) to call the methods, and property binding [disabled] to conditionally disable the 'Previous' button.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two navigation buttons appear in the step content container: 'Previous' and 'Next'. The 'Previous' button is disabled on the first step.
successCriteria: The 'Previous' button calls previousStep on click and is disabled when currentStepIndex is 0. The 'Next' button calls nextStep on click.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the navigation buttons with proper click handlers and conditional disabling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the buttons, but check that the 'Previous' button is properly disabled on the first step and both buttons have the correct click handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation buttons are missing or not properly configured. Make sure you have both 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons with (click) handlers and [disabled] binding for 'Previous'.

steps.title: Add form fields to first step
steps.instruction: Inside the step content container, add two input fields for name and email using [(ngModel)] binding. Place them within the first step's content area.
steps.hint: Use <input> elements with type="text" and type="email". Bind them to component properties using [(ngModel)] and add appropriate labels.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first step will display name and email input fields with two-way data binding.
successCriteria: Two input fields with [(ngModel)] binding are added to the step content container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added form fields with two-way binding to capture user input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some form fields, but make sure both name and email inputs are present with [(ngModel)] binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step content container doesn't contain the required form fields with [(ngModel)] binding.

steps.title: Add completion message
steps.instruction: Add a completion message that displays when all steps are completed. Use *ngIf to conditionally show a paragraph with a success message.
steps.hint: Check if currentStepIndex equals the last step index (steps.length - 1) to determine when to show the completion message.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditionally showing a message

All steps completed successfully!
steps.expectedOutcome: A completion message appears when the user reaches the final step, providing feedback that all steps are completed.
successCriteria: A paragraph with a success message is conditionally rendered using *ngIf when currentStepIndex equals the last step index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a completion message that appears when all steps are finished, providing clear feedback to the user.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the completion message only shows when the user is on the final step. Check your *ngIf condition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The completion message isn't appearing correctly. Remember to use *ngIf with a condition that checks if currentStepIndex equals steps.length - 1.
